q: We define superintelligent software engineering as the discipline of building and evolving software with agents whose capability exceeds that of human engineers
r: IC1: governance position paper with a small context-file staleness measurement and no evaluation of coding agents or of an SDD or context mechanism; doubt excludes.

q: We analyzed 2,870 instruction-file pull requests across 2,246 repositories.
r: Include: empirical study of how agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md) are reviewed, group (b), full paper from 2026.

q: We conducted a formative study with 12 developers
r: Include: agent memory and configuration files for coding agents managed by developers, with a controlled study measuring task performance on full-stack projects, group (b).

q: The dataset covers 4,738 repositories across five tools
r: Include: full dataset paper of context files, skills, rules and hooks for agentic coding tools, group (b).

q: We collect and analyze over 12,110 .cursorrules files from 11,427 GitHub repositories
r: Include: empirical mixed-methods study of Cursor rule files, group (b), full paper from 2026.

q: we analyze 15,549 agentic PRs from 148 projects in the AIDev dataset
r: Include: measures the effect of instruction files on agent pull-request merge rate, churn and effort, group (b), RQ4.

q: agentic prompts grow nearly monotonically, more than tripling over their lifetime
r: Include: empirical and experimental study of CLAUDE.md growth and prompt maintenance for coding agents, group (b).

q: We measure their effect on 21 models in single answers and on four agents in a sandbox
r: Include: measures effect and cost of SKILL.md revisions on coding agents, group (b), RQ2 and RQ4.
